front: Explain the mental model of Chain of Responsibility (how the system thinks).
back: Ordered checks: auth → goal → page → creative → budget. Each handler does one job; on success calls next, on failure short-circuits with an error. Open for extension: append a handler without editing others.

front: What is Abstract Factory in one sentence?
back: Create families of related products without binding to concrete classes — Dive Into Design Patterns (Marketing platform = campaign + adset + creative + ad + insights).

front: Explain the mental model of Abstract Factory (how the system thinks).
back: When products must match as a set (Meta campaign service with Meta adset service — never mix Meta + Google mid-pipeline), declare one factory interface with a create method per product. Each platform gets one concrete factory that returns the whole consistent family.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Abstract Factory?
back: New platform → new *MarketingFactory + register in Design pattern/Factory Method. Existing Meta factory and call sites stay closed.

front: When should you NOT use Abstract Factory?
back: Only one platform and no second planned — concrete services at composition root. Products are independent and never used as a matched set — separate factories / DI bindings.

front: What is Static members (class-level state and methods) in one sentence?
back: Belong to the type, not instances — one shared slot in memory; no virtual dispatch; common for factories, constants, and caches; abuse causes test pain and hidden global state.

front: What is Strategy pattern in one sentence?
back: Family of interchangeable algorithms behind one interface — pick at runtime — Dive Into Design Patterns + ODAX/goal configs in Marketing API.

front: Explain the mental model of Strategy pattern (how the system thinks).
back: Encapsulate what varies. When behavior branches by type (payment gateway, campaign goal, compression codec), put each variant in its own class implementing a shared interface. The context holds a strategy reference and delegates — no switch sprayed through the codebase.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Strategy pattern?
back: Context ──holds──► Strategy (interface) → GoalLeads GoalCalls GoalVisits

front: Given a broken Strategy pattern setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Context ──holds──► Strategy (interface)

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Strategy pattern?
back: 1. Add NewGoalStrategy implementing the interface. 2. Register in GOAL_STRATEGIES. 3. Do not edit existing strategies or sprinkle if (goal === 'new').

front: Symptom: Still editing switches in 5 files — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Bypass / forgotten registry · Fix: One resolve function; ban raw switches

front: Symptom: New goal needs core changes — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Interface too thin or too fat · Fix: Widen strategy API or split strategies (System Design/SOLID ISP)

front: Symptom: Wrong config at runtime — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Bad registry key / default · Fix: Fail closed on unknown id

front: Symptom: Strategies share 80% code — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Copy-paste · Fix: Shared helpers module — not a mega base class

front: Symptom: Tests couple to Meta fields — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Strategy returns vendor DTOs · Fix: Return domain config; Design pattern/Adapter translates

front: Gotcha with Strategy pattern: what silently fails?
back: Inheritance for reuse is the classic smell Strategy replaces: one superclass, override everywhere, change ripples to all subclasses.

front: When should you NOT use Strategy pattern?
back: One algorithm, no planned variants. Variants differ only by data (config object / lookup table), not behavior.

front: What is Template Method in one sentence?
back: Fixed algorithm skeleton in a base class (or function); subclasses override steps — Dive Into Design Patterns + LaunchPipeline.

front: Explain the mental model of Template Method (how the system thinks).
back: Launch always: validate → create campaign → create adset → create creative → create ad → publish events. Platforms differ in *how* each step talks to the vendor. Template Method locks the order; overrides supply platform-specific steps.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Template Method?
back: LaunchPipeline.run() → validate() ← may use Chain → createCampaign() ← override per platform → createAdSet() → createCreative()

front: Given a broken Template Method setup, what is your first validation command?
back: LaunchPipeline.run()

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Template Method?
back: Favor composition when steps themselves are strategies — hybrid is common (pipeline + goal strategy).

front: Symptom: Copy-paste launch flows per platform — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No shared skeleton · Fix: Extract Template Method base

front: Symptom: Base knows Meta fields — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Leakage · Fix: Steps use factory + adapter only

front: Symptom: Optional step forced — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Abstract when optional · Fix: Default empty hook (afterLaunch)

front: Symptom: Hard to test mid-step — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Monolith run · Fix: Test concrete step overrides with fake factory

front: Gotcha with Template Method: what silently fails?
back: Deep Template Method hierarchies reintroduce the inheritance pain Strategy was meant to avoid — keep one base + one level of concretes.

front: When should you NOT use Template Method?
back: Steps are identical — one function, no inheritance. Only one step varies — Design pattern/Strategy pattern or a callback hook.

front: What is Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance) in one sentence?
back: Same-named method on outer and inner type — which implementation runs depends on the static type of the reference, not the "logical" OOP hierarchy; source of subtle bugs in Go embedding and Java hiding.

front: Explain the mental model of Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance) (how the system thinks).
back: Overriding (Java virtual methods) — dynamic dispatch on runtime type.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance)?
back: Go embed: var c Car; c.Start() → Car.Start if defined, else promoted Engine.Start → Java static: Child.hide() hides Parent.hide — reference type picks method → Java field: Child.x shadows Parent.x — no polymorphism on fields

front: Given a broken Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Go embed: var c Car; c.Start() → Car.Start if defined, else promoted Engine.Start

front: Symptom: Wrong Log/helper called — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Go promoted vs outer method · Fix: Qualify embed s.Logger.Log or rename

front: Symptom: Java "override" doesn't run — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Method static / private / wrong sig · Fix: Remove static; match signature; add @Override

front: Symptom: Unexpected field value — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Field shadowing · Fix: Rename field; use getter

front: Symptom: Interface default vs class — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Java 8+ default methods · Fix: Explicit override in impl

front: Symptom: LSP violation in tests — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Shadowing breaks substitutability · Fix: Favor composition over inheritance

front: Gotcha with Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance): what silently fails?
back: Go is not Java — no subclass polymorphism on embedded structs; outer method is fixed at compile time for that type.

front: When should you NOT use Method shadowing (embedding / inheritance)?
back: Inheritance to reuse one method — prefer explicit delegation (golang/go embedding with named field). Shadowing fields intentionally — code smell; rename for readability.
